strategy: normative-first; follow actual source hyperlinks to algorithms

facts.claim: a[href] represents a hyperlink; button type selects activation behavior. Missing/invalid type is Auto with command/commandfor and select-parent exceptions.

Native disabled is presence-based, includes a first-legend exception for disabled fieldsets, suppresses user-interaction queued clicks and bars constraint validation; it does not prohibit all programmatic or indirect value changes.
Entry-list construction skips disabled fields. readonly is not itself an exclusion; other inclusion rules still apply. readonly does not apply to checkbox/button controls.

ARIA in HTML permits aria-disabled instead of disabled on appropriate buttons with necessary functional scripting; disabled plus aria-disabled=false is prohibited. aria-disabled semantics apply to focusable descendants.

showModal activates HTML document blocking/inertness outside the topmost modal dialog and flat-tree descendants. aria-modal describes modal semantics; authors must make the interface operable through modal descendants.

HTML dialog guidance selects meaningful autofocus; tabindex on dialog is prohibited. Removing open manually bypasses close behavior. Close restoration depends on previous modality/current focus location.
WCAG 4.1.2 requires programmatically determinable name/role and appropriate state/value setting/change notification. Its native-control note is limited to that success criterion.

proposed_contract.classification: design proposal derived from sources; not an additional normative standard

rules.action: Prefer the matching native element; set type=button for non-submit button operations. Do not add duplicate keyboard activation without a single-execution check.
Use native disabled where applicable. Check inherited disabled state and the intended entry-list consequences. Do not mirror redundant/conflicting ARIA.

rules.input: unavailable; explicit requirement to remain discoverable in tab order
rules.action: For an appropriate button, use aria-disabled only with a shared canExecute guard on all exposed execution routes. Focus retention is an input choice, not mandatory for all unavailable controls.

rules.input: not editable but value still relevant
rules.action: Use readonly only on applicable controls; record display value, current DOM value and submitted data separately. Do not infer business policy from the attribute.

Use connected dialog showModal/close lifecycle, meaningful autofocus and close-event synchronization. Provide upstream logical fallback when invoker cannot receive focus. Cancellation must use upstream policy.
Use nonmodal behavior; do not apply background inertness or a modal focus loop. Do not forcibly restore when the user has moved focus outside a nonmodal dialog.

counterexamples.rule_falsified: All controls become read-only by setting readonly
disabled and readonly have interchangeable form semantics
counterexamples.case: A required immutable identifier becomes disabled and disappears from FormData
Styled panel declares aria-modal but background is still operable

counterexamples.rule_falsified: Always focus the first button or first field
counterexamples.case: A readonly identifier or close button precedes the intended editable field

counterexamples.rule_falsified: A disabled control cannot change its value
counterexamples.case: Script sets value or a peer radio changes its checkedness indirectly

counterexamples.rule_falsified: Every dialog close should focus its invoker
counterexamples.case: User moved outside a nonmodal dialog before it closes

tests.steps: Activate an available native button once with pointer, Enter and Space; count committed actions.
tests.falsifier: Any route commits 0 or more than 1 actions, or unexpectedly submits an unrelated form.

tests.steps: For both native-disabled and explicitly discoverable aria-disabled modes, attempt pointer, Enter, Space and exposed shortcut routes.
tests.falsifier: canExecute=false yet any route commits an action.

tests.steps: Compare name/value-matched enabled, readonly and disabled controls with editing and FormData; keep other inclusion conditions equal.
tests.falsifier: Readonly remains user-editable, or disabled/readonly are serialized identically contrary to the requested mapping; readonly checkbox is treated as protected.

tests.steps: Compare a control in the first legend and one outside that legend in a disabled fieldset.
tests.falsifier: All descendants are assumed disabled uniformly, or own .disabled is treated as the full effective-state test.

tests.steps: Open modal, verify chosen focus, traverse both directions, cancel using the supported exit, reopen.
tests.falsifier: Background page control receives focus/activation, cancellation commits, state remains open after native close, or no meaningful initial focus exists.

tests.steps: Open modal, remove invoker, close modal and inspect actual activeElement.
tests.falsifier: Fallback is absent/unusable or focus restoration is reported successful despite failing.

tests.steps: Open nonmodally, move to a background input, close the dialog.
tests.falsifier: Background is inert/trapped or closing steals focus from that input.
Stale handler, DOM attribute, open state or ARIA state disagrees with input policy.
